cells.tense: You are holding steady while you point the way through, and the pointing comes from what you know.
cells.act: make something skilled and small on the cleared ground
cells.ask: Take what you understood when the old structure fell, and make a small, skilled version of it this week. One real piece on the cleared ground, done carefully, not a plan for later.
cells.core:
When someone can't see the way, you find it with them and stay steady while they get their feet under them. That isn't coldness. It's tested — you don't point at passages you haven't walked.

The insight that took the old shape down left ground behind it. That ground is where something new gets built, and building is skilled work: a piece at a time, done carefully. Pick a piece and do it well enough that it stands. The endurance that carries you across hard crossings is the same thing that makes what you build stay built. Nothing here needs to be finished; it needs to be real.

cells.tense: You are bracing to chart a crossing no one has reached yet, and the bracing is outrunning the moment.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Pick the hardest piece of what you're pushing toward, and walk straight into it. Not forcing anything — just meeting it directly. Then watch what holds and what bends, and let that tell you the truth.
cells.core:
Guiding well looks like waiting for the passage to open, then pointing at it — from knowledge you've actually tested. Right now you're already charting a crossing nobody's reached, and the bracing has taken the place of the waiting.

Friction is how this finds its level again. Walk into the hard part and find out what actually stands. What you're committed to will survive being tested; what you've been forcing past its moment won't. Let go of the method that's straining, keep the purpose that's yours. The test isn't outlasting something that keeps bending — it's whether the commitment itself is sound.

cells.tense: You stood at a passage that was already behind you, and you have not gone through.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: There's a small unfairness near you. Do the right thing about it quietly — no credit, no mentioning it afterward. Just the act itself, and let that be the end of it.
cells.core:
Guiding well looks like walking a passage yourself and then showing it to someone — you know the ground because you've crossed it. Right now you see where the passage is and you're standing at a door that closed behind you. Holding on without moving has become holding still.

What's needed isn't more effort. It's a small fair act, taken on the private sense you already carry. Near you is a case where the right thing is plain. Do that. It doesn't ask for energy you don't have or a feeling you can't summon. One step taken on what's fair, and the rest follows the way water finds its bed.

cells.tense: The passage people follow through you is being charted, and the one charting it says they aren't.
cells.act: let the vision be shared with one other
cells.ask: Bring the direction you're carrying alone to someone who hasn't seen it — not the whole of it, the part you've kept back — and let the two of you run it together from there.
cells.core:
People find their way through what you already worked out. They lean on how you hold, and the route they follow was charted by you, quietly, without your name on it. By your own account you were just standing nearby. The ones you guided would laugh at that.

The move here is toward connection, not more solitary carrying. Take a piece you've been holding by yourself and share it — one person, in the open, as yours. You don't have to claim everything you've built. Claim a piece of it out loud to someone who will receive it. The vision runs better once it stops being a private load.
